html:
SMTO-UI-0054 — SMTO couldn't check one part of the system

GUID: 38a260e4-6a6b-50a1-9898-de78ba58097e
Slug: ui-health-check-failed
Domain: UI · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO tried to check the status of one part of the system but got no answer. That doesn't mean the part is broken, and the other checks still count.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open System Health (select Open System Health if this message shows it) and find the card marked Status unavailable. That card is the part of SMTO that couldn't be checked.
  2. Select that card's check button, such as Check Knowledge or its Refresh button. A status check only reads information, so running it again is safe and may succeed now.
  3. If it still says Status unavailable, open Diagnostic summary on that card and select Copy diagnostic summary. The summary records what went wrong for whoever manages SMTO.

What success looks like

  • The card shows a current result such as Check passed or Needs attention instead of Status unavailable.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied diagnostic summary and the error details (select Copy error details) to the person who manages SMTO. Keep using the parts of SMTO that work; this failed check alone doesn't mean they're affected.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A System Health probe for one component could not produce a current observation (the check failed or returned no usable status); the other components' checks are independent and remain valid.

What this means

  • The app could not obtain a current observation for one component. Other successful checks remain useful. The original operation and completed work retain their own recorded outcomes; this diagnostic does not replay them.

Why this can happen

  • The component reported ui_health_check_failed. This does not establish the outcome of unrelated operations.

How to diagnose it

  • The affected check returns a current observation.
  • Inspect the error reference and the affected component’s current observation before selecting a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Open System Health (/system-health), rerun the affected component's check (Check Knowledge, or that card's Refresh button) and read its Diagnostic summary and the Server log for the underlying exception. No current code path emits ui_health_check_failed directly (System Health shows Status unavailable on the card instead), so treat an occurrence as coming from an older page. Keep the original error details; the failed check does not establish that other features are unavailable.
  • Open System Health and inspect the affected component. Keep the original error details; the failed check does not establish that other features are unavailable.

Retry and execution caution

  • The affected check returns a current observation.

How to verify the fix

  • The affected check returns a current observation.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Status checks do not replay tasks or modify source documents.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
